title.raw: 卷31 于栗磾 Volume 31: Yu Lidi

sentences.zh: 于栗磾

translations.literal: Yu Lidi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lidi

sentences.zh: 于栗磾，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Lidi was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lidi came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 能左右馳射，武藝過人。

translations.literal: He could shoot while galloping to left and right, and his martial arts surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: He could shoot from horseback at full gallop in either direction, and his martial prowess was exceptional.

sentences.zh: 登國中，拜冠軍將軍，假新安子。

translations.literal: During the Dengguo era he was appointed Champion General and given the provisional title Marquis of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dengguo period he was made Champion General and granted the provisional title Marquis of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 後與寧朔將軍公孫蘭領步騎二萬，潛自太原從韓信故道開井陘路，襲慕容寶於中山。

translations.literal: Later, together with Pacification-of-the-North General Gongsun Lan, he led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry, secretly from Taiyuan along Han Xin's old route to open the Jingxing Pass road and attack Murong Bao at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Pacification-of-the-North General Gongsun Lan commanded twenty thousand foot and horse, stole from Taiyuan along Han Xin's old line to reopen the Jingxing route, and struck Murong Bao at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 既而車駕後至，見道路修理，大悅，即賜其名馬。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived afterward and he saw the roads repaired, he was greatly pleased and at once bestowed on him famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived afterward and saw the roads in good repair, he was delighted and immediately rewarded Lidi with prized horses.

sentences.zh: 及趙魏平定，太祖置酒高會，謂栗磾曰：「卿即吾之黥彭。

translations.literal: When Zhao and Wei were pacified, Emperor Taizu set out wine at a grand gathering and said to Lidi, "You are my Ying Bu and Peng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao and Wei were pacified, Emperor Taizu held a great banquet and told Lidi, "You are my Ying Bu and Peng Yue rolled into one.

sentences.zh: 」大賜金帛，進假新安公。

translations.literal: " He gave him a great gift of gold and silk and advanced his provisional title to Duke of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: " He lavished gold and silk on him and promoted his provisional title to Duke of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 太祖田於白登山，見熊將數子，顧謂栗磾曰：「卿勇幹如此，寧能搏之乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu was hunting on Mount Bai and saw a bear leading several cubs; turning to Lidi he said, "With courage and strength like yours, could you wrestle it?
translations.idiomatic: While hunting on Mount Bai, Emperor Taizu saw a bear with several cubs and asked Lidi, "A man as bold and capable as you—could you take that beast in a fight?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「天地之性，人為貴。

translations.literal: " He replied, "In the nature of Heaven and Earth, man is the noblest.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "In Heaven and Earth's order, human life is what matters most.

sentences.zh: 若搏之不勝，豈不虛斃一壯士。

translations.literal: If one wrestles and does not win, would that not waste a brave warrior's life in vain?
translations.idiomatic: If I fought and lost, would that not throw away a good soldier for nothing?

sentences.zh: 自可驅致御前，坐而制之。

translations.literal: One may simply drive it to come before Your Majesty and subdue it while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Better to drive it before you and take it at your leisure.

sentences.zh: 」尋皆擒獲。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward they were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he had captured them all.

sentences.zh: 太祖顧而謝之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu turned and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned and thanked him for the lesson.

sentences.zh: 永興中，關東羣盜大起，西河反叛。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era bandits rose in great numbers east of the Pass, and Xihe rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxing, bandit armies swarmed through the east of the Pass and Xihe rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 栗磾受命征伐，所向皆平，即以本號留鎮平陽。

translations.literal: Lidi received orders to campaign; wherever he went all was pacified, and he was left to garrison Pingyang with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi took command on campaign and swept all before him; he was then left to hold Pingyang under his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 轉鎮遠將軍，河內鎮將，賜爵新城男。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pacifier-of-the-Distance General and garrison commander of Henei, and enfeoffed as Baron of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Pacifier-of-the-Distance General and garrison commander of Henei, with the barony of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 栗磾撫導新邦，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Lidi guided and comforted the new territories and had great authority combined with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi governed the newly won lands with a firm hand and real benevolence.

sentences.zh: 劉裕之伐姚泓也，栗磾慮其北擾，遂築壘於河上，親自守焉。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Lidi feared he would harass the north and therefore built fortifications on the river and personally defended them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched against Yao Hong, Lidi feared a northern incursion and built river fortifications, guarding them in person.

sentences.zh: 禁防嚴密，斥候不通。

translations.literal: Prohibitions and defenses were strict; scouts could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: His blockade was tight; no scout could pass.

sentences.zh: 裕甚憚之，不敢前進。

translations.literal: Yu greatly feared him and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu held him in deep respect and would not push north.

sentences.zh: 裕遺栗磾書，遠引孫權求討關羽之事，假道西上，題書曰「黑矟公麾下」。

translations.literal: Yu sent Lidi a letter, citing at length how Sun Quan had asked to attack Guan Yu in order to request passage westward; he addressed the letter "To the camp of the Duke of the Black Spear."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu wrote to Lidi, invoking at length Sun Quan's request to strike Guan Yu as precedent for a western passage, and addressed the letter "To the camp of the Duke of the Black Spear."

sentences.zh: 栗磾以狀表聞，太宗許之，因授黑矟將軍。

translations.literal: Lidi reported the matter in a memorial; Emperor Taizong approved and thereupon appointed him Black Spear General.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi reported this to the throne; Emperor Taizong agreed and created him Black Spear General.

sentences.zh: 栗磾好持黑矟以自標，裕望而異之，故有是語。

translations.literal: Lidi liked to carry a black spear as his mark; Yu saw it from afar and found it remarkable, hence this wording.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi was known for bearing a black spear as his badge; Liu Yu had noticed it from afar, which explains the epithet.

sentences.zh: 奚斤之征虎牢也，栗磾別率所部攻德宗河南太守王涓之於金墉，涓之棄城遁走。

translations.literal: When Xi Jin campaigned against Hulao, Lidi separately led his command to attack Dade's Administrator of Henan Wang Juanzhi at Jinyong; Juanzhi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: During Xi Jin's siege of Hulao, Lidi led his own force against Dade's Henan administrator Wang Juanzhi at Jinyong; Juanzhi abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 遷豫州刺史，將軍如故，進爵新安侯。

translations.literal: He was moved to Governor of Yuzhou with his generalship unchanged and advanced in rank to Marquis of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Yuzhou at the same general's rank and raised to Marquis of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 洛陽雖歷代所都，久為邊裔，城闕蕭條，野無煙火。

translations.literal: Although Luoyang had been the capital of successive dynasties, for long it had been a frontier region; towers and gates were desolate and in the countryside there was no hearth smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had been capital to dynasty after dynasty, yet it had long lain on the frontier—its walls and gates were hollow, and no smoke rose from the fields.

sentences.zh: 栗磾刊闢榛荒，勞來安集。

translations.literal: Lidi cleared and opened the brambles and waste, and with labor and summons brought people to settle.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi cut back the wilderness, called people home, and settled them in peace.

sentences.zh: 德刑既設，甚得百姓之心。

translations.literal: Once virtue and punishment were established, he won the hearts of the common people greatly.
translations.idiomatic: With law and mercy in place, he won the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 太宗南幸盟津，謂栗磾曰：「河可橋乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong traveled south to Meng Ford and said to Lidi, "Can the river be bridged?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong went south to Meng Ford and asked Lidi, "Can we bridge this river?

sentences.zh: 」栗磾曰：「杜預造橋，遺事可想。

translations.literal: " Lidi said, "When Du Yu built a bridge, the precedent remains to be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: " Lidi replied, "Du Yu once bridged a river—the precedent is there to follow.

sentences.zh: 」乃編次大船，構橋於冶坂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he arrayed large boats in sequence and built a bridge at Yebankou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then lashed great boats together and threw a bridge across at Yebankou.

sentences.zh: 六軍既濟，太宗深歎美之。

translations.literal: Once the six armies had crossed, Emperor Taizong sighed in deep admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the whole army had crossed, Emperor Taizong praised him with deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 世祖之征赫連昌，敕栗磾與宋兵將軍、交趾侯周幾襲陝城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, he ordered Lidi together with Song-Bing General and Marquis of Jiaozhi Zhou Ji to strike Shan City.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Shizu's campaign against Helian Chang, he ordered Lidi and Song-Bing General, Marquis of Jiaozhi Zhou Ji, to take Shan City by surprise.

sentences.zh: 昌弘農太守曹達不戰而走。

translations.literal: Chang's Administrator of Hongnong Cao Da fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's Hongnong administrator Cao Da fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 乘勝長驅，仍至三輔。

translations.literal: Riding the victory they drove far and still reached the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the victory in a long pursuit all the way into the Three Metropolises.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，加安南將軍。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to duke and he was given the additional title Pacifier of the South General.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to duke and made Pacifier of the South General as well.

sentences.zh: 平統萬，遷蒲坂鎮將。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified, he was transferred to garrison commander of Puban.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongwan fell, he was posted as garrison commander of Puban.

sentences.zh: 時弘農、河內、上黨三郡賊起，栗磾討之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in the three commanderies of Hongnong, Henei, and Shangdang; Lidi suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels broke out in Hongnong, Henei, and Shangdang, Lidi put them down.

sentences.zh: 轉虎牢鎮大將，加督河內軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to great garrison commander of Hulao and given supervision over the Henei army.
translations.idiomatic: He became great garrison commander of Hulao with oversight of the Henei forces.

sentences.zh: 尋遷使持節、都督兗相二州諸軍事、[1]鎮南將軍、枋頭都將。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yan and Xiang provinces, [1] Pacifier of the South General, and Chief Commander of Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Bearer of the Staff, commander of all forces in Yan and Xiang, Pacifier of the South General, and chief commander at Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 又為外都大官，平刑折獄，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He also served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court; in settling punishments and deciding cases he had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court, where his judgments won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 賜東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the Eastern Garden funeral regalia, one set of court dress, and a full suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 栗磾自少治戎，迄于白首，臨事善斷，所向無前。

translations.literal: From youth Lidi managed military affairs; until his white head, in facing affairs he was good at decision and wherever he went none stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi had soldiered from youth to white hair; in action he decided swiftly and nothing stood in his path.

sentences.zh: 加以謙虛下士，刑罰不濫。

translations.literal: Moreover he was modest and lowered himself toward gentlemen; punishments were not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest with his men and never abused the lash.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu deeply mourned and cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 子洛拔，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Luoba inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoba inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少以功臣子，拜侍御中散。

translations.literal: In youth, as the son of a meritorious minister, he was appointed Attendant Imperial Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man, being a meritorious minister's son, he was made Attendant Imperial Scribe.

sentences.zh: 有姿容，善應對，恭慎小心。

translations.literal: He had a fine appearance, was skilled in repartee, and was respectful, cautious, and careful.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome, quick in conversation, and unfailingly respectful and careful.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚加愛寵，因賜名焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu greatly favored and doted on him and therefore bestowed a name on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu favored him greatly and gave him his personal name.

sentences.zh: 車駕征討，恒在侍衞，擢領監御曹事。

translations.literal: On imperial campaigns he was always in attendance as guard and was promoted to head the Bureau of Imperial Guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he rode in the imperial guard and was put in charge of the Bureau of Imperial Escort.

sentences.zh: 從征涼州，既平，賜奴婢四十口，轉監御曹令。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign to Liangzhou; when it was pacified he was given forty male and female servants and transferred to Director of the Bureau of Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Liangzhou campaign and, after its pacification, received forty household slaves and was made director of the Bureau of Imperial Escort.

sentences.zh: 恭宗之在東宮，厚加禮遇，洛拔以恭宗雖則儲君，不宜逆自結納，恒畏避屏退，左轉領候宮曹事。

translations.literal: When Gongzong was in the Eastern Palace he treated Luoba with great courtesy; Luoba held that although Gongzong was the heir, one ought not presumptuously to bind oneself to him, and always feared, avoided, and withdrew; he was demoted to the left to head the Bureau of Palace Waiting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzong was crown prince he showered Luoba with favor, but Luoba felt that even a heir apparent was not someone with whom a subject should court private ties; he kept his distance and was shifted to head the palace waiting office instead.

sentences.zh: 頃之，襲爵。

translations.literal: Before long he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、散騎常侍、寧東將軍、和龍鎮都大將、營州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Pacifier of the East General, Chief Great Commander of Helong Garrison, and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Pacifier of the East General, chief commander of the Helong garrison, and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以治有能名，進號安東將軍。

translations.literal: Because his governance had a reputation for ability, his title was advanced to Pacifier of the East General.
translations.idiomatic: His able administration won him promotion to Pacifier of the East General.

sentences.zh: 又為外都大官。

translations.literal: He again served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 會隴西屠各王景文等恃險竊命，私署王侯，高宗詔洛拔與南陽王惠壽督四州之眾討平之，徙其惡黨三千餘家於趙魏。

translations.literal: It happened that the Tuge kings Jingwen and others of Longxi relied on rugged terrain to usurp authority and privately appointed kings and marquises; Emperor Gaozong ordered Luoba together with Prince of Nanyang Huishou to command the forces of four provinces to suppress and pacify them, and relocated more than three thousand households of their wicked faction to Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Longxi Tuge chiefs such as Wang Jingwen seized the highlands and set up their own lords, Emperor Gaozong ordered Luoba and Prince of Nanyang Huishou to lead four provinces' troops against them; more than three thousand rebel households were relocated to Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 轉拜侍中、殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing while remaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Masters of Writing while keeping his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 在朝祗肅，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: In court he was reverent and solemn; the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In court he was grave and disciplined, and the officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 太安四年卒，時年四十四。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tai'an at age forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tai'an, at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 洛拔有六子。

translations.literal: Luoba had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba had six sons.

sentences.zh: 長子烈，善射，少言，有不可犯之色。

translations.literal: The eldest son Lie was skilled in archery, spoke little, and had an air that could not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Lie was a fine archer, sparing of speech, with a bearing no one cared to cross.

sentences.zh: 少拜羽林中郎，遷羽林中郎將。

translations.literal: In youth he was appointed Central Commander of the Feathered Forest and was promoted to General of the Central Command of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered the Feathered Forest as a central commander and rose to general of that guard.

sentences.zh: 延興初，敕領寧光宮宿衞事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanxing he was ordered to head the night guard affairs of Ningguang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanxing he was ordered to command the night guard of Ningguang Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷屯田給納。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Garrison Fields Provision Supply.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of garrison-field provisions.

sentences.zh: 太和初，秦州刺史尉洛侯，雍州刺史、宜都王目辰，長安鎮將陳提等，貪殘不法，烈受詔案驗，咸獲贓罪，洛侯、目辰等皆致大辟，提坐徙邊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Qinzhou Inspector Wei Luohou, Yongzhou Inspector and Prince of Yidu Muchen, Chang'an Garrison Commander Chen Ti, and others were greedy, cruel, and lawless; Lie received orders to investigate; all were found guilty of embezzlement; Luohou, Muchen, and others were all put to death, while Ti was sentenced to exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe, Qinzhou inspector Wei Luohou, Yongzhou inspector and Prince of Yidu Muchen, Chang'an garrison commander Chen Ti, and others were corrupt and lawless; Lie was ordered to investigate them. All were convicted of graft; Luohou, Muchen, and others were executed, and Ti was banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 仍以本官行秦雍二州事。

translations.literal: He still held his former office and acted for the affairs of Qin and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his rank while acting for Qin and Yong provinces.

sentences.zh: 遷司衞監，總督禁旅。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Palace Guards and supervised the forbidden troops in general.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the palace guards with overall command of the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 從幸中山，車駕還次肆州，司空苟頹表沙門法秀詃惑百姓，潛謀不軌，詔烈與吏部尚書

translations.literal: He followed on the imperial visit to Zhongshan; when the carriage returned and halted at Si Province, Minister of Works Gou Tui memorialized that the monk Faxiu had deluded the common people and secretly plotted sedition; an edict ordered Lie together with the Minister of the Masters of Writing for Official Personnel
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Zhongshan; on the return the court halted at Si Province, where Minister of Works Gou Tui reported that the monk Faxiu was misleading the people and plotting rebellion. An edict ordered Lie and the Minister of the Masters of Writing for Official Personnel

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 丞祖馳驛討之。

translations.literal: Chengzu to ride post-horses in haste to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu to ride post-haste and suppress the plot.

sentences.zh: 會秀已平，轉左衞將軍，賜爵昌國子。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiu had already been pacified; he was transferred to General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: Faxiu had already been crushed; Lie was made General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書，賜帛三千匹。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Palace Secretariat and granted three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Secretariat and given three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 于時高祖幼冲，文明太后稱制，烈與元丕、陸叡、李沖等各賜金策，許以有罪不死。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu was young and Empress Dowager Wenming held power; Lie together with Yuan Pi, Lu Rui, Li Chong, and others were each granted golden tablets, with permission that if guilty they would not die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still a child and Empress Dowager Wenming ruled in his name; Lie, Yuan Pi, Lu Rui, Li Chong, and others each received a golden writ promising that no capital crime would take their lives.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，遷前將軍，進爵洛陽侯。

translations.literal: He was given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, moved to Forward General, and advanced in rank to Marquis of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, promoted to Forward General, and raised to Marquis of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋轉衞尉卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，加鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the southern campaign and was given the additional title Pacifier of the South General.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was made Pacifier of the South General as well.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛陽，人情戀本，多有異議，高祖問烈曰：「卿意云何？

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, people's feelings clung to their native region and many had objections; Emperor Gaozu asked Lie, "What is your view?
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Luoyang, many clung to the old capital and murmured against the change; Emperor Gaozu asked Lie, "What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」烈曰：「陛下聖略淵遠，非愚管所測。

translations.literal: " Lie said, "Your Majesty's sacred design is deep and far-reaching; it is not what this foolish office can fathom.
translations.idiomatic: " Lie said, "Your Majesty's design is too deep for a man like me to judge.

sentences.zh: 若隱心而言，樂遷之與戀舊，唯中半耳。

translations.literal: If I speak from the hidden heart, joy in the move and attachment to the old are only half and half.
translations.idiomatic: If I speak honestly, half the people welcome the move and half mourn the old home.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿既不唱異，即是同，深感不言之益。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said, "Since you do not lead the dissent, that is agreement; I deeply feel the benefit of your not speaking out.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You are not leading the opposition—that is support enough. I am grateful for your restraint.

sentences.zh: 宜且還舊都，以鎮代邑。

translations.literal: You should for the time return to the old capital to secure the Dai region.
translations.idiomatic: Return for now to the old capital and hold the Dai homeland firm.

sentences.zh: 」敕留臺庶政，一相參委。

translations.literal: " He ordered that all routine administration left at the secondary capital be entrusted to him in full.
translations.idiomatic: " He left him in charge of all government at the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸代，執烈手曰：「宗廟至重，翼衞不輕，卿當祗奉靈駕，時遷洛邑。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Dai, he took Lie's hand and said, "The ancestral temple is supremely weighty and its guard is no light matter; you should reverently escort the spirit carriage and in due time move it to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Dai, he took Lie's hand and said, "The ancestral temple is the weightiest charge and its guard no light duty. Escort the spirit tablets reverently and bring them to Luoyang in due time.

sentences.zh: 朕以此事相託顧，非不重也。

translations.literal: I entrust this matter to your care; it is not that I do not regard it as weighty.
translations.idiomatic: I am entrusting this to you—not because it is a small matter.

sentences.zh: 」烈與高陽王雍奉遷神主於洛陽，高祖嘉其勳誠，遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: " Lie together with Prince of Gaoyang Yong reverently moved the spirit tablets to Luoyang; Emperor Gaozu praised his merit and loyalty and moved him to Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: " Lie and Prince of Gaoyang Yong brought the spirit tablets to Luoyang; the emperor praised their loyal service and made Lie Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 十九年，大選百僚，烈子登引例求進。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, in the great selection of the hundred officials, Lie's son Deng cited precedent to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, during the great civil-service selection, Lie's son Deng cited precedent to seek promotion.

sentences.zh: 烈表曰：「臣上或近臣，下不決引一人，

translations.literal: Lie submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant, being either a superior or a close minister, below has not once decided to recommend a single person,
translations.idiomatic: Lie memorialized: "Your servant, whether as a superior or a close minister at court, has never once chosen to recommend anyone below,

translations.literal: Text doubtful in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful or missing text in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 而恩出分外，冀荷榮祿。

translations.literal: yet favor has gone beyond the norm, hoping to bear glory and salary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he seeks favor beyond his due and hopes for rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 當今聖明之朝，理應謙讓，而臣子登引人求進，是臣素無教訓，請乞黜落。

translations.literal: In the present sage and enlightened court, one ought to be modest and yield; yet my son Deng has had someone recommend him to seek advancement—this shows your servant has long lacked instruction; I beg to be dismissed and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In so enlightened a court he ought to have known humility; instead my son Deng had himself put forward for promotion. That shows I have failed to teach him. I beg to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「此乃有識之言，不謂烈能辦此。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said, "These are words of discernment; I did not expect Lie could do this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "That is the speech of a man of sense—I did not think Lie capable of it.

sentences.zh: 」乃引見登，詔曰：「朕今創禮新邑，明揚天下，卿父乃行謙讓之表，而有直士之風，故進卿為太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he summoned Deng for an audience and decreed, "I now establish rites in the new capital and raise the worthy throughout the realm; your father has submitted a memorial of modest yielding and has the manner of an upright man—therefore I advance you to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned Deng and said, "I am founding a new capital and seeking talent across the land. Your father has just shown the humility of a true gentleman, so I promote you to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.

sentences.zh: 」又加烈散騎常侍，封聊城縣開國子，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: " He also gave Lie the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Liaocheng with an established fief, and granted a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " He also made Lie Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed him as founding viscount of Liaocheng county with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及穆泰、陸叡謀反舊京，高祖幸代，泰等伏法。

translations.literal: When Mu Tai and Lu Rui plotted rebellion at the old capital, Emperor Gaozu visited Dai; Tai and the others were executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Tai and Lu Rui plotted rebellion at the old capital, Emperor Gaozu went to Dai; Tai and his fellows were executed.

sentences.zh: 賜烈及李沖璽書，述金策之意。

translations.literal: He granted Lie and Li Chong sealed letters stating the meaning of the golden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lie and Li Chong sealed letters recalling the promise of the golden writs.

sentences.zh: 語在陸叡傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Lu Rui.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Lu Rui.

sentences.zh: 是逆也，代鄉舊族，同惡者多，唯烈一宗，無所染預。

translations.literal: This was treason; the old clans of the Dai region had many fellow evildoers, but Lie's clan alone had no stain of involvement.
translations.idiomatic: It was treason, and many old families of Dai were implicated—but Lie's house alone was untouched.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其忠操，益器重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised his loyal integrity and valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised his loyalty and relied on him still more heavily.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「元儼決斷威恩，深自不惡，然而為臣盡忠猛決，不如烈也。

translations.literal: He sighed and said, "Yuan Yan is decisive in authority and favor and is by no means contemptible in himself, yet in serving as minister with full loyalty, fierceness, and decision he does not equal Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "Yuan Yan is formidable in judgment and favor and no mean man—but as a minister utterly loyal, fierce, and decisive, he cannot match Lie.

sentences.zh: 爾日烈在代都，必即斬其五三元首耳。

translations.literal: Had Lie been at the Dai capital that day, he would at once have beheaded the ringleaders among the five or three clans.
translations.idiomatic: If Lie had been in Dai that day, he would have cut down the rebel leaders on the spot.

sentences.zh: 烈之節概，不謝金日磾也。」

translations.literal: Lie in integrity of conduct does not yield to Jin Midi."
translations.idiomatic: Lie in moral fiber is the equal of Jin Midi."

sentences.zh: 詔除領軍將軍。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him General of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Palace Guards by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 以本官從征荊沔，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: With his former office he followed the campaign to Jing and Mian and was given an additional suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Jing-Mian campaign in the same rank and was granted a military band.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂彭城王勰曰：「烈先朝舊德，智勇兼有，軍之大計，宜共參決。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "Lie is an old worthy of the former court, possessing both wisdom and courage; on the great plans of the army you should deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "Lie is a veteran of the previous reign, wise and brave alike—you should share in every major military decision.

sentences.zh: 」宛鄧既平，車駕還洛，論功加散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " When Wan and Deng were pacified, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang; for merit he was given the additional posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: " After Wan and Deng fell, the emperor returned to Luoyang and rewarded him with Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，蕭寶卷遣其太尉陳顯達入寇馬圈，高祖輿疾赴之，執烈手曰：「都邑空虛，維捍宜重。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Xiao Baojuan sent his Grand Commandant Chen Xianda to invade Maquan; Emperor Gaozu went despite illness and took Lie's hand, saying, "The capital is empty; its defense must be weighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, Xiao Baojuan's Grand Commandant Chen Xianda invaded Maquan; though ill, Emperor Gaozu went in person and took Lie's hand. "The capital is nearly bare," he said. "Its defense is paramount.

sentences.zh: 可鎮衞二宮，以輯遠近之望。

translations.literal: You may secure and guard the two palaces to settle the hopes of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the two palaces and steady the hopes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」顯達破走，高祖崩於行宮，彭城王勰總一六軍，祕諱而返，稱詔召世宗會駕魯陽。

translations.literal: " Xianda was defeated and fled; Emperor Gaozu died at the traveling palace; Prince of Pengcheng Xie commanded the whole army, kept the death secret, and returned, proclaiming an edict summoning Emperor Shizong to meet the carriage at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianda was routed, but the emperor died at the field palace. Prince of Pengcheng Xie took command of the army, concealed the death, and marched back under orders summoning Emperor Shizong to meet the coffin at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 以烈留守之重，密報凶問。

translations.literal: Because of the weight of Lie's duty as defender, the grievous news was reported to him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Lie, left to guard the capital, was told the news in secret.

sentences.zh: 烈處分行留，神色無變。

translations.literal: Lie disposed of remaining affairs and his expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Lie settled what remained to be done without a change in his bearing.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，寵任如前。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, favor and trust were as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, Lie enjoyed the same favor as before.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧為宰輔，權重當時，曾遣家僮傳言於烈曰：「須舊羽林虎賁執仗出入，領軍可為差遣。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi was chief minister; his authority weighed heavily in the age; he once sent a household slave with a message to Lie saying, "I need the old Feathered Forest tiger guards to bear arms in going in and out; the Commander of the Guards may dispatch them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang Xi, the chief minister, wielded enormous power. He once sent a servant to Lie with this message: "I need veteran Feathered Forest guards armed for my comings and goings—the Commander of the Guards can supply them.

sentences.zh: 」烈曰：「天子諒闇，事歸宰輔，領軍但知典掌宿衞，有詔不敢違，理無私給。

translations.literal: " Lie said, "The Son of Heaven is in mourning and affairs belong to the chief minister; the Commander of the Guards only knows how to manage night guard duty—where there is an edict I dare not disobey, but by principle there is no private allotment.
translations.idiomatic: " Lie replied, "The emperor is in mourning and affairs rest with the chief minister. I command only the palace guard—I obey edicts, but I do not hand out troops on private request.

sentences.zh: 」奴惘然而返，傳烈言報禧。

translations.literal: " The slave returned in bewilderment and relayed Lie's words to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: " The servant went back baffled and reported Lie's answer to Xi.

sentences.zh: 禧復遣謂烈曰：「我是天子兒，天子叔，元輔之命，與詔何異？

translations.literal: Xi again sent word to Lie, saying, "I am the Son of Heaven's son and the Son of Heaven's uncle; the chief minister's command—how does it differ from an edict?
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent again: "I am the emperor's son and uncle. A chief minister's order—is it not as good as an edict?

sentences.zh: 」烈厲色而答曰：「向者亦不道王非是天子兒、叔。

translations.literal: " Lie with stern countenance replied, "Earlier I did not say Your Highness was not the Son of Heaven's son and uncle.
translations.idiomatic: " Lie answered coldly, "I never denied that you are the emperor's son and uncle.

sentences.zh: 若是詔，應遣官人，所由遣私奴索官家羽林，[2]烈頭可得，羽林不可得！

translations.literal: If it were an edict, officials should be sent; as it is, a private slave was sent to demand the court's Feathered Forest—[2] Lie's head may be obtained, but the Feathered Forest may not!
translations.idiomatic: If it were an edict, you would send an officer—not a household slave to demand the imperial guard. [2] You may have my head, but you will not have the guard!

sentences.zh: 」禧惡烈剛直，遂議出之，乃授使持節、散騎常侍、征北將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: " Xi hated Lie's stern uprightness and thereupon discussed removing him; he was then given Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Campaign North General, and Governor of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi hated Lie's inflexibility and arranged to send him away, appointing him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Campaign North General, and Governor of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 烈不願藩授，頻表乞停，輒優答弗許。

translations.literal: Lie did not wish for a provincial appointment and repeatedly memorialized begging to be excused; each time a gracious reply refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: Lie did not want a provincial post and memorialized repeatedly to decline; each time the court graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 烈乃謂彭城王勰曰：「殿下忘先帝南陽之詔乎？

translations.literal: Lie then said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "Has Your Highness forgotten the late emperor's command at Nanyang?
translations.idiomatic: Lie then said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "Have you forgotten the late emperor's charge at Nanyang?

sentences.zh: 而逼老夫乃至於此。

translations.literal: Yet you drive this old man to this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you drive an old man this far.

sentences.zh: 」遂以疾固辭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " He then pleaded illness and refused outright.

sentences.zh: 世宗以禧等專擅，潛謀廢之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Xi and others were domineering and arbitrary, secretly plotted to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, finding Xi and his faction overbearing, secretly planned to strip them of power.

sentences.zh: 會二年正月礿祭，[3]三公並致齋於廟，世宗夜召烈子忠謂曰：「卿父忠允貞固，社稷之臣。

translations.literal: It happened that in the first month of the second year was the Yue sacrifice;[3] the Three Excellencies all kept fast at the temple; at night Emperor Shizong summoned Lie's son Zhong and said, "Your father's loyalty, fairness, and steadfast integrity make him a pillar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year came the Yue sacrifice;[3] the Three Excellencies were fasting at the ancestral temple. That night the emperor summoned Lie's son Zhong and said, "Your father is loyal, upright, and steadfast—a true pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 明可早入，當有處分。

translations.literal: Tomorrow enter early; there will be orders.
translations.idiomatic: Come early tomorrow—you will receive your orders.

sentences.zh: 」忠奉詔而出。

translations.literal: " Zhong received the command and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong withdrew with his orders.

sentences.zh: 質明，烈至，世宗詔曰：「諸父慢怠，漸不可任，今欲使卿以兵召之，卿其行乎？

translations.literal: At dawn Lie arrived; Emperor Shizong decreed, "The imperial uncles are negligent and slack and gradually cannot be entrusted; I now wish you to summon them with troops—will you go?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Lie came in. The emperor said, "My uncles have grown negligent and can no longer be trusted. I want you to summon them at sword-point. Will you go?

sentences.zh: 」烈對曰：「老臣歷奉累朝，頗以幹勇賜識。

translations.literal: " Lie replied, "This old minister has served successive courts and has been known somewhat for capacity and courage.
translations.idiomatic: " Lie answered, "I have served several reigns and am known, such as I am, for resolve and courage.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Today's affair is what I dare not decline.
translations.idiomatic: I will not refuse today's task.

sentences.zh: 」乃將直閣已下六十餘人，宣旨召咸陽王禧、彭城王勰、北海王詳，衞送至于帝前。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led more than sixty men from the Direct Attendants downward, proclaimed the imperial will to summon Prince of Xianyang Xi, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, and Prince of Beihai Xiang, and escorted them under guard before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " He took more than sixty men of the Direct Attendants and below, proclaimed the summons to Princes Xi of Xianyang, Xie of Pengcheng, and Xiang of Beihai, and escorted them under guard to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諸公各稽首歸政。

translations.literal: The princes each bowed with forehead to the ground and returned their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince kowtowed and surrendered his powers.

sentences.zh: 以烈為散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、領軍，進爵為侯，增邑三百戶，并前五百戶。

translations.literal: Lie was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of the Guards; his rank was advanced to marquis; his fief was increased by three hundred households, making five hundred together with the former.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of the Guards, raised to marquis with three hundred added households for a total of five hundred.

sentences.zh: 自是長直禁中，機密大事，皆所參焉。

translations.literal: From then on he kept long duty in the palace; on confidential great affairs he was all consulted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he kept constant watch in the palace and was consulted on every secret matter of state.

sentences.zh: 太尉、咸陽王禧謀反也，武興王楊集始馳於北邙以告。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion; Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi galloped to Northern Mang to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion; Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi rode post-haste to Northern Mang to warn the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時世宗從禽於野，左右分散，直衞無幾，倉卒之際，莫知計之所出。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Shizong was hunting in the wilds; attendants were scattered and direct guards were few; in the sudden crisis none knew what plan to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was hunting; his attendants were scattered and his guard thin. In the sudden alarm no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 乃敕烈子忠馳覘虛實。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Lie's son Zhong to ride in haste to observe the true situation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lie's son Zhong to ride ahead and learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 烈時留守，已處分有備，因忠奏曰：「臣雖朽邁，心力猶可，此等猖狂，不足為慮。

translations.literal: Lie was then on guard duty and had already made dispositions and preparations; through Zhong he memorialized, saying, "Your servant, though decayed and aged, still has strength of mind; such reckless arrogance is not worth anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Lie, left in charge, had already made his dispositions. Through Zhong he reported: "I am old, but my wits still serve. This rabble is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 願緩蹕徐還，以安物望。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to slow the carriage and return at ease to settle the expectations of all.
translations.idiomatic: Return at your leisure to steady the court and the people.

sentences.zh: 」世宗聞之，甚以慰悅。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Shizong heard this, he was greatly comforted and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 及駕還宮，禧已遁逃。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the palace, Xi had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the emperor reached the palace, Xi had already fled.

sentences.zh: 詔烈遣直閤叔孫侯將虎賁三百人追執之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lie to send Direct Attendant Shusun Hou to lead three hundred tiger guards in pursuit to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was ordered to send Direct Attendant Shusun Hou with three hundred tiger guards to run Xi down and capture him.

sentences.zh: 順后既立，以世父之重，彌見優禮。

translations.literal: After Empress Shun was established, because of the weight of his position as imperial uncle he was all the more treated with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Shun was enthroned, Lie as the emperor's senior uncle received still greater honor.

sentences.zh: 八月，暴疾卒，時年六十五。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he died suddenly of illness at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he died suddenly, at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 世宗舉哀於朝堂，給東園第一祕器，朝服一具，衣一襲；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong mourned him in the audience hall, granted the first-grade secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothing;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong mourned him in the audience hall and granted the highest-grade Eastern Garden funeral regalia, one set of court dress, and a full suit of robes;

sentences.zh: 賜錢二百萬，布五百匹；

translations.literal: granted two million in cash and five hundred bolts of cloth;
translations.idiomatic: two million in cash and five hundred bolts of cloth;

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、大將軍、太尉公、雍州刺史；

translations.literal: posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Governor of Yongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: posthumously Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Governor of Yongzhou;

sentences.zh: 追封鉅鹿郡開國公，增邑五百戶，并前千戶。

translations.literal: posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Julu commandery with an established fief, fief increased by five hundred households, making one thousand together with the former.
translations.idiomatic: and posthumously enfeoffed as founding duke of Julu commandery with five hundred added households for a total of one thousand.

sentences.zh: 烈有五子。

translations.literal: Lie had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lie had five sons.

sentences.zh: 長子祚，字萬年。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zuo, style Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Zuo, courtesy name Wannian.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為中散，稍遷恒州別駕。

translations.literal: During Taihe he served as Palace Scribe and was gradually moved to Aide of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was a palace scribe and later became aide of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 除假節、振威將軍、沃野鎮將，貪殘多所受納。

translations.literal: He was appointed with provisional staff, Quelling Might General, and garrison commander of Woye; he was greedy and cruel and took many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was made provisional staff-bearer, Quelling Might General, and garrison commander of Woye, where he was greedy, cruel, and took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 坐免官，以公還第。

translations.literal: For this he was dismissed from office and returned to his residence as a duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and sent home as a duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祚子若，襲爵。

translations.literal: Zuo's son Ruo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's son Ruo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 多酒過，為叔父景所撾殺。

translations.literal: He had many faults of drunkenness and was beaten to death by his uncle Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He drank to excess and was beaten to death by his uncle Jing.

sentences.zh: 子順襲。

translations.literal: His son Shun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shun inherited.

sentences.zh: 卒，子馥襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Fu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Fu inherited.

sentences.zh: 祚弟忠，字思賢，本字千年。

translations.literal: Zuo's younger brother Zhong, style Sixian, original style Qiannian.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Sixian, originally Qiannian.

sentences.zh: 弱冠拜侍御中散。

translations.literal: At weak cap he was appointed Attendant Imperial Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was made Attendant Imperial Scribe.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，刑政頗峻，侍臣左右，多以微譴得罪。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, punishments and administration were quite severe; attendants at the emperor's side often offended over small faults.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Wenming's regency justice was harsh, and many court attendants fell for minor slips.

sentences.zh: 忠朴直少言，終無過誤。

translations.literal: Zhong was plain, upright, and sparing of speech; to the end he had no errors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was plain, upright, and quiet, and never once gave offense.

sentences.zh: 太和中，授武騎侍郎，因賜名登。

translations.literal: During Taihe he was appointed Gentleman of the Martial Cavalry and was thereupon granted the name Deng.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he became Gentleman of the Martial Cavalry and received the personal name Deng.

sentences.zh: 轉太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷長水校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was moved to Commandant of the Ever-Flowing Waters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he was made Commandant of the Ever-Flowing Waters.

sentences.zh: 尋除左右郎將，[4]領直寢。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Left and Right and [4] headed the Direct Guard of the Bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General of the Left and Right [4] and placed in charge of the imperial bedchamber guard.

sentences.zh: 元禧之謀亂也，車駕在外，變起倉卒，未知所之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xi plotted disorder, the imperial carriage was abroad; the crisis arose suddenly and none knew where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xi rebelled, the emperor was away hunting; the crisis came suddenly and no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 忠進曰：「臣世蒙殊寵，乃心王室。

translations.literal: Zhong advanced and said, "Your servant's house has received exceptional favor for generations; my heart is with the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong stepped forward and said, "My family has enjoyed extraordinary favor for generations; my heart is with the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣父領軍，付留守之重計，防遏有在，必無所慮。

translations.literal: My father the Commander of the Guards was entrusted with the weight of the defense; measures to block and restrain are in place—there is surely nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: My father commands the guard and was left in charge; he will have made every provision—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」世宗即遣忠馳騎觀之，而烈分兵嚴備，果如所量。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong at once sent Zhong riding in haste to observe; Lie had divided troops and made strict preparations—indeed it was as estimated.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Zhong at once to see; Lie had already deployed his forces—and all was exactly as Zhong had said.

sentences.zh: 世宗還宮，撫背曰：「卿差強人意。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong returned to the palace, he patted his back and said, "You are rather satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the palace the emperor clapped his shoulder and said, "You did well.

sentences.zh: 」賜帛五百匹。

translations.literal: " He granted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「先帝賜卿名登，誠為美稱，朕嘉卿忠款，今改卿名忠。

translations.literal: He also said, "The late emperor granted you the name Deng, truly a fine designation; I praise your loyal sincerity and now change your name to Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The late emperor named you Deng—a fine name. I honor your loyalty and now rename you Zhong.

sentences.zh: 既表貞固之誠，亦所以名實相副也。」

translations.literal: This both displays steadfast integrity and makes name and reality match."
translations.idiomatic: It marks your steadfast loyalty and makes the name fit the man."

sentences.zh: 父憂去職。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起復本官。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 遷司空長史。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 于時太傅、錄尚書、北海王詳親尊權重，將作大匠王遇多隨詳所欲而給之。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Prince of Beihai Xiang was close, honored, and weighty in power; the Master of Works Wang Yu often supplied whatever Xiang desired.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Prince of Beihai Xiang was powerful and close to the throne; Master of Works Wang Yu supplied his every whim.

sentences.zh: 後因公事，忠於詳前謂遇曰：「殿下國之周公，阿衡王室，所須材用，自應關旨，何至阿諛附勢，損公惠私也。

translations.literal: Later on public business, Zhong before Xiang said to Yu, "Your Highness is the state's Duke of Zhou, supporting and balancing the imperial house; materials needed should naturally go through proper channels—how can you reach flattery and cling to power, harming the public and favoring the private?
translations.idiomatic: Later, on official business, Zhong said to Wang Yu in Xiang's presence: "His Highness is the state's Duke of Zhou; whatever he needs should pass through proper channels. Why fawn on power and rob the public purse for private ends?

sentences.zh: 」遇既不寧，詳亦慚謝。

translations.literal: " Yu was ill at ease, and Xiang also apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu was uneasy; Xiang apologized in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Campaign Barbarians General; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Campaign Barbarians General; his other duties were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以平元禧功，封魏郡開國公，食邑九百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Yuan Xi he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei commandery with an established fief, fief of nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing Yuan Xi's rebellion he was enfeoffed as founding duke of Wei commandery with nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍，兼武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 每以鯁氣正辭，為北海王詳所忿，面責忠曰：「我憂在前見爾死，不憂爾見我死時也。

translations.literal: Because he always spoke with sturgeon-spine spirit and upright words, he incurred the resentment of Prince of Beihai Xiang, who face to face rebuked Zhong, saying, "I worry about seeing you die first; I do not worry about you seeing me when I die.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt honesty angered Prince of Beihai Xiang, who confronted him: "I worry about outliving you, not about you outliving me.

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「人生於世，自有定分，若應死於王手，避亦不免；

translations.literal: " Zhong said, "Life in the world has its allotted portion; if one ought to die by Your Highness's hand, even fleeing cannot escape;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong replied, "Each man's span is fixed. If I am fated to die by your hand, flight will not save me;

sentences.zh: 若其不爾，王不能殺。

translations.literal: if it is not so, Your Highness cannot kill me.
translations.idiomatic: if not, you cannot kill me.

sentences.zh: 」詳因忠表讓之際，密勸世宗以忠為列卿，令解左右，聽其讓爵。

translations.literal: " Xiang, taking advantage of Zhong's memorial of yielding, secretly urged Emperor Shizong to make Zhong a ranked minister, have him relinquish his attendance at the side, and allow him to yield his title.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang used Zhong's memorial of modesty to urge the emperor to promote him to the ranks of ministers, strip him of his post at court, and let him surrender his title.

sentences.zh: 於是詔停其封，優進太府卿。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict halted his enfeoffment and graciously advanced him to Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The court halted his enfeoffment and promoted him to Director of the Imperial Treasury instead.

sentences.zh: 正始二年秋，詔忠以本官使持節、兼侍中，為西道大使，刺史、鎮將贓罪顯暴者，以狀申聞，守令已下，便即行決。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Zhengshi, an edict ordered Zhong with his former office as Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Palace Attendant to serve as envoy of the western circuit; where governors and garrison commanders had manifest crimes of embezzlement, he was to report in memorial; for magistrates and below he might execute judgment on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the second year of Zhengshi, Zhong was ordered as Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Palace Attendant to serve as envoy on the western circuit. Where governors and garrison commanders were openly corrupt, he was to report to the throne; for county and district officials he could pass sentence on the spot.

sentences.zh: 與撫軍將軍、尚書李崇分使二道。

translations.literal: Together with Pacification Army General and Master of Writing Li Chong he divided the mission into two circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He and Pacification Army General and Master of Writing Li Chong divided the empire between them on two routes.

sentences.zh: 忠劾并州刺史高聰贓罪二百餘條，論以大辟。

translations.literal: Zhong impeached Bingzhou Inspector Gao Cong on more than two hundred counts of embezzlement and argued for death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong impeached Bingzhou inspector Gao Cong on more than two hundred counts of graft and argued for execution.

sentences.zh: 還，除平西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Pacifier of the West General and Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Pacifier of the West General and Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，不行。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his stepmother and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was mourning his stepmother and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授安北將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Pacifier of the North General and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Pacifier of the North General and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又為衞尉卿，河南邑中正。

translations.literal: He again served as Commandant of the Guards and Rectifier of Henan district.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Commandant of the Guards and as rectifier of the Henan district.

sentences.zh: 詔忠與吏部尚書元暉、度支尚書元匡、河南尹元萇等推定代方姓族。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhong together with Minister of the Masters of Writing for Official Personnel Yuan Hui, Minister of Revenue Yuan Kuang, Intendant of Henan Yuan Chang, and others to determine the clans of the Dai region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was ordered, together with Minister of Personnel Yuan Hui, Minister of Revenue Yuan Kuang, Intendant of Henan Yuan Chang, and others, to fix the ranking of Dai-region clans.

sentences.zh: 高肇忌其為人，欲密出之，乃言於世宗，稱中山要鎮，作捍須才，以忠器能，宜居其位。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao resented his character and wished secretly to send him out; he spoke to Emperor Shizong, saying that Zhongshan was a vital garrison, defense required talent, and because of Zhong's capacity he should fill that post.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao disliked him and wanted him out of court; he told Emperor Shizong that Zhongshan was a key garrison needing a capable defender and that Zhong was the man for the post.

sentences.zh: 於是出授安北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out and appointed Pacifier of the North General and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was sent out as Pacifier of the North General and Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗既而悔之，復授衞尉卿，領左衞將軍、恒州大中正。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong afterward regretted it and again appointed him Commandant of the Guards, heading the Left Guard General and Grand Rectifier of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted it and recalled him as Commandant of the Guards, with the Left Guard and as grand rectifier of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 密遣中使詔曰：「自比股肱褫落，心膂無寄。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent a palace envoy with a decree saying, "Of late my arms and legs have been stripped away; my heart and backbone have nowhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent a palace messenger with these words: "Lately I have lost my right arms; I have no one to lean on.

sentences.zh: 方任雖重，比此為輕。

translations.literal: Though the post in the regions is weighty, compared with this it is light.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial post is weighty, but lighter than what I need from you.

sentences.zh: 故輟茲外任，委以內務。

translations.literal: Therefore I set aside that outer appointment and entrust you with inner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: So I am ending your service abroad and entrusting you with affairs at court.

sentences.zh: 當勤夙無怠，稱朕所寄也。

translations.literal: You should be diligent from dawn without slackening, to match what I entrust.
translations.idiomatic: Work from dawn without slackening—that is what I ask of you."

sentences.zh: 」延昌初，除都官尚書，加平南將軍，領左衞、中正如故。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Yanzhang he was appointed Minister of Justice, given the additional title Pacifier of the South General, and retained the Left Guard and rectifier posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanzhang he was made Minister of Justice and Pacifier of the South General, keeping the Left Guard and his rectifier duties.

sentences.zh: 又加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was also given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嘗因侍宴，賜之劍杖，舉酒屬忠曰：「卿世秉貞節，故恒以禁衞相委。

translations.literal: Once at a banquet in attendance he granted him sword and staff, raised his cup and addressed Zhong, saying, "Your house for generations has held steadfast integrity; therefore I constantly entrust you with the forbidden guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet he gave Zhong sword and staff, raised his cup, and said, "Your family has served with integrity for generations—that is why I always trust you with the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 昔以卿行忠，賜名曰忠。

translations.literal: Formerly because of your conduct of loyalty I granted you the name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: I named you Zhong for your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今以卿才堪禦侮，以所御劍杖相賜。

translations.literal: Now because your talent can repel insult I bestow the sword and staff I myself use.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because your talent can repel insult, I give you the sword and staff I carry myself.

sentences.zh: 循名取義，意在不輕。

translations.literal: Following the name to take the meaning—the intent is not light.
translations.idiomatic: Name and gift match; do not take this lightly.

sentences.zh: 其出入周旋，恒以自防也。

translations.literal: In going out and coming in and in your rounds, constantly use them for your own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Carry them whenever you move about the palace."

sentences.zh: 」忠頓首陳謝。

translations.literal: " Zhong bowed with forehead to the ground and expressed thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、領軍將軍，忠面陳讓云：「臣無學識，不堪兼文武之任。

translations.literal: He was moved to Palace Attendant and General of the Palace Guards; Zhong face to face declined, saying, "Your servant lacks learning and knowledge and cannot bear the joint burden of civil and military duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and General of the Palace Guards. Zhong declined to his face: "I lack learning and am unfit for both civil and military command.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「當今學識有文者不少，但心直不如卿。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said, "Today there are not a few men of learning and literary skill, but none as straight of heart as you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Men of learning are not rare, but none are as straight-hearted as you.

sentences.zh: 欲使卿劬勞於下，我當憂無於上。」

translations.literal: I wish you to toil below so that I need not worry above."
translations.idiomatic: I want you to bear the labor below so that I need not worry above."

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，夜中與侍中崔光遣右衞將軍侯剛迎肅宗於東宮而即位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, in the night he together with Palace Attendant Cui Guang sent Right Guard General Hou Gang to welcome Emperor Suzong from the Eastern Palace and install him on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong died, Zhong and Palace Attendant Cui Guang sent Right Guard General Hou Gang that night to bring Emperor Suzong from the Eastern Palace to the throne.

sentences.zh: 忠與門下議，以肅宗幼年，未親機政；

translations.literal: Zhong deliberated with the Secretariat, holding that Suzong was young and had not yet personally handled state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the Secretariat agreed that Suzong was young and had not yet taken the reins himself;

sentences.zh: 太尉、高陽王雍屬尊望重，宜入居西柏堂，省決庶政；

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince of Gaoyang Yong was close kin, honored, and weighty in prestige and should enter and dwell in the Western Cypress Hall to review and decide routine administration;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Prince of Gaoyang Yong, eminent and close to the throne, should enter the Western Cypress Hall and decide routine government;

sentences.zh: 任城王澄明德茂親，可為尚書令，總攝百揆。

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng Cheng was of bright virtue and flourishing kinship and could serve as Director of the Masters of Writing, overseeing all departments.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Cheng, virtuous and of imperial blood, should be Director of the Masters of Writing and oversee all ministries.

sentences.zh: 奏中宮，請即敕授。

translations.literal: They memorialized the inner palace, requesting immediate edict and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized the inner palace for immediate orders.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉王顯欲逞姦計，與中常侍、給事中孫伏連等厲色不聽，寢門下之奏。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian wished to carry out a treacherous plot; together with Regular Palace Attendant and Bearer of the Inner Gate Sun Fulian and others he with stern countenance refused to listen and shelved the Secretariat's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian meant to carry out a treacherous plot; with Regular Palace Attendant Sun Fulian and others he refused to listen and blocked the Secretariat's memorial.

sentences.zh: 宮

translations.literal: The palace
translations.idiomatic: The palace

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 侍中、黃門，但牒六輔姓字齎來。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants and Yellow Gate officials were only to bring lists of the six ministers' names and styles.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants and Yellow Gate officials were told only to bring lists of the six ministers' names.

sentences.zh: 孫伏連等密欲矯太后令，以高肇錄尚書事，顯與高猛為侍中。

translations.literal: Sun Fulian and others secretly wished to forge the empress dowager's order, making Gao Zhao Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with Xian and Gao Meng as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fulian and others secretly meant to forge the empress dowager's order making Gao Zhao Recorder of the Masters of Writing and appointing Xian and Gao Meng as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 忠即於殿中收顯殺之。

translations.literal: Zhong at once seized Xian in the hall and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong seized Xian in the hall and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 忠既居門下，又總禁衞，遂秉朝政，權傾一時。

translations.literal: Zhong, having taken the Secretariat and also commanding the forbidden guard, thereupon held court administration; his power tilted the age.
translations.idiomatic: With the Secretariat and the palace guard in his hands, Zhong ruled the court and for a time his power knew no rival.

sentences.zh: 初，太和中軍國多事，高祖以用度不足，百官之祿四分減一。

translations.literal: Initially, during Taihe the state and army had many affairs; Emperor Gaozu because expenditures were insufficient reduced all officials' salaries by one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe, with war and state expenses heavy, Emperor Gaozu had cut all official salaries by one quarter.

sentences.zh: 忠既擅權，欲以惠澤自固，乃悉歸所減之祿，職人進位一級。

translations.literal: Zhong, having seized power, wished to secure himself with favors and therefore fully restored the reduced salaries and advanced every officeholder one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, Zhong sought to buy loyalty by restoring the full salaries and promoting every officeholder one rank.

sentences.zh: 舊制：天下之民絹布一匹之外，各輸綿麻八兩。

translations.literal: Old regulation: beyond one bolt of silk cloth per household, the people of the realm each paid eight ounces of cotton and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, beyond one bolt of silk cloth per household, every taxpayer also owed eight ounces of cotton and hemp.

sentences.zh: 忠悉以與之。

translations.literal: Zhong gave all of this to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong remitted all of this as well.

sentences.zh: 忠白高陽王雍，自云世宗本許優轉。

translations.literal: Zhong informed Prince of Gaoyang Yong, saying himself that Emperor Shizong had originally promised him preferential advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong told Prince of Gaoyang Yong that Emperor Shizong had promised him a special promotion.

sentences.zh: 雍憚忠威權，便順其意，加忠車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Yong feared Zhong's authority and power and followed his wish, adding for Zhong the title General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong feared Zhong's power and went along, making him General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 忠自謂新故之際，有安社稷之功，諷動百僚，令加己賞。

translations.literal: Zhong considered that at the transition between old and new he had merit in securing the altars of state; he prompted the hundred officials and had them add to his reward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong believed he had saved the dynasty at the succession and pressed the officials to reward him.

sentences.zh: 於是太尉雍、清河王懌、廣平王懷難違其意，議封忠常山郡開國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Commandant Yong, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and Prince of Guangping Huai found it hard to oppose his wish; they deliberated enfeoffing Zhong as Duke of Changshan commandery with an established fief, fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yong, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and Prince of Guangping Huai dared not refuse; they proposed enfeoffing Zhong as founding duke of Changshan commandery with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 百僚咸以為然。

translations.literal: The hundred officials all considered it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The officials all assented.

sentences.zh: 忠又難於獨受，乃諷朝廷，同在門下者皆加封邑。

translations.literal: Zhong again found it hard to accept alone and therefore prompted the court that all who shared the Secretariat should receive increased fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to take the reward alone, Zhong had everyone in the Secretariat given enlarged fiefs as well.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射郭祚、尚書裴植以忠權勢日盛，勸雍出忠。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Guo Zuo and Master of Writing Pei Zhi, because Zhong's power grew daily, urged Yong to send Zhong out.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Guo Zuo and Master of Writing Pei Zhi, alarmed at Zhong's growing power, urged Yong to send him away.

sentences.zh: 忠聞之，逼有司誣奏其罪。

translations.literal: When Zhong heard this, he compelled the relevant offices to frame memorials accusing them of crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong heard of this and forced the authorities to frame charges against them.

sentences.zh: 郭祚有師傅舊恩，裴植擁地入國，忠並矯詔殺之。

translations.literal: Guo Zuo had old favor as tutor; Pei Zhi had brought territory into the state; Zhong forged edicts and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo had been tutor to the emperor; Pei Zhi had surrendered territory to the state—Zhong forged edicts and had them both killed.

sentences.zh: 朝野憤怨，莫不切齒，王公已下，畏之累跡。

translations.literal: Court and countryside burned with resentment; none did not gnash teeth; from kings and dukes downward all feared him and walked in his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country seethed with hatred; princes and officials alike walked in fear of him.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺高陽王雍，侍中崔光固執，乃止，遂免雍太尉，以王還第。

translations.literal: He also wished to kill Prince of Gaoyang Yong; Palace Attendant Cui Guang firmly resisted and he stopped; thereupon Yong was removed as Grand Commandant and returned to his residence as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also tried to kill Prince of Gaoyang Yong, but Palace Attendant Cui Guang stood firm against it; Yong was merely stripped of the Grand Commandancy and sent home.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，詔命生殺，皆出於忠。

translations.literal: From this time onward, edicts, orders, life, and death all issued from Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, edicts of life and death issued from Zhong alone.

sentences.zh: 既尊靈太后為皇太后，居崇訓宮，忠為儀同三司、尚書令、領崇訓衞尉，侍中、領軍如故。

translations.literal: After Empress Ling was honored as empress dowager and dwelt in Chongxun Palace, Zhong was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, and head of Chongxun Commandant of the Guards, with Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Ling was made empress dowager and moved to Chongxun Palace, Zhong became Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, and head of the Chongxun guard, retaining Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，解忠侍中、領軍、崇訓衞尉，止為儀同、尚書令，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court she relieved Zhong of Palace Attendant, Commander of the Guards, and Chongxun Commandant of the Guards, leaving him only Equal in Honor and Director of the Masters of Writing, with Palace Attendant added.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager took power she stripped Zhong of Palace Attendant, Commander of the Guards, and head of the Chongxun guard, leaving him Equal in Honor and Director of the Masters of Writing with Palace Attendant restored.

sentences.zh: 忠為令旬餘，靈太后引門下侍官于崇訓宮，問曰：「忠在端右，聲聽何如？

translations.literal: Zhong had been director for little more than ten days when Empress Dowager Ling summoned Secretariat attendants to Chongxun Palace and asked, "Zhong at the chief post—how is his reputation and hearing?
translations.idiomatic: After barely ten days as director, the empress dowager summoned Secretariat officials to Chongxun Palace and asked, "How is Zhong doing in the chief post?

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：「不稱厥位。

translations.literal: " All said, "He does not match his position.
translations.idiomatic: All answered, "He is not fit for the office.

sentences.zh: 」乃出忠使持節、都督冀定瀛三州諸軍事、征北大將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zhong was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces, Campaign North Grand General, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: She sent Zhong out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Ji, Ding, and Ying, Campaign North Grand General, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 太傅清河王等奏曰：「竊惟先帝升遐之初，皇上登極之始，四海謐然，宇內晏清。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe and others memorialized, saying, "We consider that at the beginning when the late emperor ascended on high and at the start when the present emperor took the pinnacle, the four seas were tranquil and within the realm all was peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe and others memorialized: "At the late emperor's death and the new emperor's accession, the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 至於奉迎乘輿，侍衞省闥，斯乃臣子之常節，職司之恒理，不容以此為功，妄開井邑。

translations.literal: As for meeting the imperial carriage, attending and guarding the palace gates—this is the constant propriety of ministers and sons and the regular duty of offices; it cannot be made merit and fiefs opened in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the imperial carriage and guarding the palace gates are ordinary duties—not grounds for fiefs.

sentences.zh: 臣等前議所以廣建茅土者，正以畏迫威權，苟免暴戾故也。

translations.literal: The reason we earlier deliberated to extend fiefs widely was precisely that we feared coercive authority and sought only to escape violence.
translations.idiomatic: We enlarged fiefs before only because we feared Zhong's power and sought to escape his wrath.

sentences.zh: 是以中議之際，以十三日夜入為無勳。

translations.literal: Therefore in the central deliberation the entry on the night of the thirteenth was held to be without merit.
translations.idiomatic: In our deliberations we held that the events of the thirteenth night earned no merit.

sentences.zh: 唯以拒違矯令，抑黜姦回，微可褒敍。

translations.literal: Only in resisting forged orders and suppressing wicked factions was there slight ground for praise.
translations.idiomatic: Only resisting forged orders and suppressing traitors deserved slight praise.

sentences.zh: 以前侍中臣忠總攝文武，侍中臣光久在樞密，讚同其意，故唯賞二人。

translations.literal: Because former Palace Attendant Zhong oversaw civil and military affairs and Palace Attendant Guang had long been in confidential posts and agreed with his intent, only these two were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhong had commanded civil and military affairs and Cui Guang, long in confidential posts, had agreed, only those two were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 今尚書臣昭等無涯上訴，奉敕重議。

translations.literal: Now Master of Writing Zhao and others appeal without limit; we receive command to deliberate again.
translations.idiomatic: Now Master of Writing Zhao and others have appealed without limit, and we are ordered to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 案王顯陰結姦徒，志為不逞；

translations.literal: We find that Wang Xian secretly joined wicked followers, his intent unrestrained;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian secretly joined traitors and meant to run riot;

sentences.zh: 高肇遠同凶逆，遙搆禍端。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao from afar shared with vicious rebels and remotely plotted the beginning of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao from afar joined the plot and stirred trouble.

sentences.zh: 無將之罪，事合洿戮。

translations.literal: The crime of failing to restrain kin clearly warranted execution.
translations.idiomatic: Their crimes warranted execution.

sentences.zh: 而忠等徵罪，唯以厥身，不至孥戮，又出罪人，窮治不盡。

translations.literal: Yet Zhong and others in punishing crimes took only their persons, did not extend to wives and children, and also released guilty men without pursuing investigation to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhong punished only the principals, spared families, released accomplices, and did not pursue the conspiracy to the end.

sentences.zh: 案律準憲，事在不輕。

translations.literal: Measured against law and statute, the matter is not light.
translations.idiomatic: By law, these failings are grave.

sentences.zh: 暨皇上纂曆，聖后別宮，母子隔異，溫清道絕，皆忠等之咎。
