translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the calendar and the sage mother dwelt in a separate palace, mother and son separated, the way of warm and pure care cut off—all were the fault of Zhong and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor succeeded, mother and son were kept apart and the rites of filial care were broken—all Zhong's doing.

sentences.zh: 過方厥勳，功微罪重。

translations.literal: Faults outweighed their merit; merit was slight and guilt heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Their faults outweighed their merit.

sentences.zh: 又忠專權之後，擅殺樞納，輒廢宰輔，令朝野駭心。

translations.literal: Moreover, after Zhong monopolized power he killed key ministers on his own authority, casually removed chief ministers, and made court and countryside hearts appalled.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing power he killed ministers on his own authority, removed chief ministers at will, and terrified the realm.

sentences.zh: 遠近怪愕。

translations.literal: Near and far were startled and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far were appalled.

sentences.zh: 功過相除，悉不合賞。

translations.literal: Merit and fault canceling each other, none of it fits reward.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and fault cancel out; none of it deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 請悉追奪。

translations.literal: We request that all be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that all rewards be revoked.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后從之。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年春，御史中尉元匡奏曰：「臣聞事主不以幽貞革心，奉上不以𧼈捨虧節。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xiping, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang memorialized, saying, "Your servant has heard that in serving one's lord one does not change heart because of seclusion and integrity, and in serving one's superiors one does not impair integrity because of hardship and abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Xiping, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang memorialized: "I have heard that a loyal servant does not change heart in seclusion, nor compromise integrity in hardship.

sentences.zh: 是以倚秦宮而慟哭，復楚之功已多；

translations.literal: Therefore leaning on the Qin palace and wailing in grief, the merit of restoring Chu was already great;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baoxu wept against the Qin palace wall and won great merit in restoring Chu;

sentences.zh: 陟盧龍而樹勤，廣魏之勳不淺。

translations.literal: ascending through Lulong and establishing merit—the achievements for expanding Wei were not shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou climbed Lulong Pass and earned no small merit for Wei;

sentences.zh: 而申包避賞，君子於是義之；

translations.literal: yet Shen Bao avoided reward, and gentlemen on this account honored his righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: yet Shen Bao refused reward, and gentlemen praised him for it;

sentences.zh: 田疇拒命，良史所以稱美。

translations.literal: Tian Chou refused orders, which good historians therefore praise.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou refused imperial orders, which good historians praise.

sentences.zh: 竊唯宮車晏駕，天人位易，正是忠臣孝子致節之秋。

translations.literal: We consider that when the imperial carriage rests in peace and Heaven and man's positions shift, it is precisely the season for loyal ministers and filial sons to offer their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor dies and the throne changes hands, it is the season for loyal ministers and filial sons to show their mettle.

sentences.zh: 前領軍將軍臣忠不能砥礪名行，自求多福，方因矯制，擅相除假，清官顯職，歲月隆崇。

translations.literal: Former Commander of the Guards Zhong could not hone his name and conduct and sought many blessings for himself; just then through forged regulations he on his own authority granted removals and provisional appointments, clear offices and prominent posts, month by month rising higher.
translations.idiomatic: Former Commander of the Guards Zhong did not hone his conduct but sought his own advantage; he forged orders, made appointments on his own authority, and month by month climbed to higher offices.

sentences.zh: 臣等在蕃之時，乃心家國，書誚往來，憤氣成疚。

translations.literal: When we were in the provinces our hearts were with the state and family; letters of blame went back and forth and indignant breath became affliction.
translations.idiomatic: When we were in the provinces our hearts were with the state; letters of protest flew back and forth and our anger became a sickness.

sentences.zh: 傷禮敗德，臣忠即主。

translations.literal: Injuring ritual and ruining virtue—Minister Zhong is the culprit.
translations.idiomatic: He injured ritual and ruined virtue—Zhong is the man responsible.

sentences.zh: 謹案臣忠世以鴻勳盛德，受遇累朝，出入承明，左右機近。

translations.literal: We respectfully find that Minister Zhong's house for generations has had great merit and flourishing virtue, receiving favor through successive courts, entering and leaving Chenming, close at the left and right of the secret machinery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's house has served with great merit for generations and enjoyed favor under successive emperors, always close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 幸國大災，肆其愚戇，專擅朝命，無人臣之心。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the state's great calamity, he indulged his foolish rashness, monopolized court commands, and had no heart of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the nation's calamity he indulged his folly, seized court authority, and showed no heart of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 裴郭受冤於既往，宰輔黜辱於明世。

translations.literal: Pei and Guo suffered injustice in the past; chief ministers were demoted and shamed in this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and Guo were wronged; chief ministers were humiliated in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 又自矯旨為儀同三司、[5]尚書令、領崇訓衞尉，原其此意，便欲無上自處。

translations.literal: Moreover he on his own forged an edict making himself Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, [5] Director of the Masters of Writing, and head of Chongxun Commandant of the Guards; tracing this intent, he wished to place himself above all.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an edict making himself Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, [5] Director of the Masters of Writing, and head of the Chongxun guard—clearly placing himself above all.

sentences.zh: 既事在恩後，宜加顯戮。

translations.literal: Since the matter comes after grace, he should receive conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: After such grace as he received, he deserves public execution.

sentences.zh: 請御史一人、令史一人，就州行決。

translations.literal: We request one censor and one clerk to go to the province and execute judgment on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that a censor and a clerk be sent to his province to execute sentence on the spot.

sentences.zh: 崔光與忠雖同受召，[6]而謂光既儒望，朝之禮宗，攝心虛遠，不關世務。

translations.literal: Cui Guang and Zhong though both received summons, [6] we hold that Guang as a Confucian luminary and the court's ritual pillar kept his mind withdrawn and distant and was not involved in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang was summoned with Zhong, [6] but as the court's ritual pillar he kept aloof from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 但忠以光意望崇重逼光，[7]光若不同，又有危禍。

translations.literal: Only Zhong, because Guang's prestige was lofty and weighty, compelled Guang; [7] if Guang had not agreed, there would again have been peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong forced Guang because of his prestige; [7] had Guang refused, he would have been in danger.

sentences.zh: 伏度二聖欽明。

translations.literal: We submit that the two sages are discerning.
translations.idiomatic: We trust that Your Majesties are discerning.

sentences.zh: 深垂昭恕。

translations.literal: They deeply extend clear pardon.
translations.idiomatic: They will extend clear pardon.

sentences.zh: 而自去歲正月十三日世宗晏駕以後，八月一日皇太后未親覽以前，諸有不由階級而權臣用命，或發門下詔書，或由中書宣敕，擅相拜授者，已經恩宥，正可免其叨竊之罪。

translations.literal: Yet from after the first day of the eighth month before the empress dowager personally reviewed affairs, back to after the thirteenth day of the first month last year when Emperor Shizong rested in peace—all who without proper rank had powerful ministers command, or issued Secretariat edicts, or had the Secretariat proclaim decrees, and on their own authority granted appointments—having already received grace may rightly be spared the crime of grasping what was not theirs.
translations.idiomatic: As for all who between the thirteenth day of the first month after Emperor Shizong's death and the first day of the eighth month before the empress dowager took power were appointed without proper procedure by powerful ministers—those already pardoned may be spared the crime of usurpation.

sentences.zh: 既非時望，朝野所知，冒階而進者，並求追奪。

translations.literal: Those who were not the hope of the age and are known to court and countryside, who advanced by usurping rank—we request that all be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: But all who advanced by usurping rank, as court and country know, should have their appointments revoked.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后令曰：「直繩所糾，實允朝憲。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling ordered, "The straight cord's corrections truly accord with court statute.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered: "The straight cord of justice has spoken rightly.

sentences.zh: 但忠事經肆宥，又蒙特原，無宜追罪。

translations.literal: But Zhong's matter has passed through great pardon and again received special grace; there is no grounds to pursue punishment.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhong has already been pardoned once and specially spared; he should not be punished further.

sentences.zh: 餘如奏。

translations.literal: The rest as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The rest as proposed.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「忠以往年大諱之際，開崇邑土。

translations.literal: " Another edict said, "Zhong at the great taboo of last year opened lofty fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Zhong received a great fief at the late emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 然酬庸理乖，有司執奪。

translations.literal: Yet the principle of rewarding merit was wrong and the relevant offices enforced revocation.
translations.idiomatic: The reward was unjust and the authorities revoked it.

sentences.zh: 豈宜一謬，棄其餘勳也。

translations.literal: How can one error discard the rest of his merit?
translations.idiomatic: One error should not cancel all his merit.

sentences.zh: 但忠厥任禁要，誠節皎然，宜褒錫山河，以安厥望。

translations.literal: Yet Zhong's post in the forbidden guard was vital; his loyal integrity was bright; he should be rewarded with mountains and rivers to settle his expectations.
translations.idiomatic: His service in the palace guard was vital and his loyalty clear; he should be rewarded with a fief to satisfy his due.

sentences.zh: 可靈壽縣開國公，邑五百戶。」

translations.literal: He may be Duke of Lingshou county with an established fief, fief of five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be founding duke of Lingshou county with five hundred households."

sentences.zh: 初，世宗崩後，高太后將害靈太后。

translations.literal: Initially, after Emperor Shizong's demise, Empress Dowager Gao planned to harm Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after Emperor Shizong died, Empress Dowager Gao intended to destroy Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 劉騰以告侯剛。

translations.literal: Liu Teng reported this to Hou Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng told Hou Gang.

sentences.zh: 剛以告忠。

translations.literal: Gang reported it to Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gang told Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠請計於崔光，光曰：「宜置胡嬪於別所，嚴加守衞，理必萬全，計之上者。

translations.literal: Zhong sought counsel from Cui Guang. Guang said: "The Hu concubine should be placed in a separate residence and strictly guarded; by reason this is entirely safe—the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong asked Cui Guang for advice. Guang said: "Place the Hu concubine in a separate residence under strict guard; that is the safest course—the best plan.

sentences.zh: 」忠等從之，具以此意啟靈太后，太后意乃安。

translations.literal: " Zhong and the others followed this, fully reported this intention to Empress Dowager Ling, and the empress dowager's mind was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the others agreed, reported the plan fully to Empress Dowager Ling, and her fears were put to rest.

sentences.zh: 故太后深德騰等四人，並有寵授。

translations.literal: Therefore the empress dowager deeply rewarded Teng and the other four men, and all received favor and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager therefore owed Teng and the other four men a deep debt, and all were favored with appointments.

sentences.zh: 忠以毀之者多，懼不免禍。

translations.literal: Because many slandered him, Zhong feared he could not escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Many spoke against him, and Zhong feared he would not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 願還京師，欲自營救。

translations.literal: He wished to return to the capital to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to the capital and save himself.

sentences.zh: 靈太后不許。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling refused.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，除尚書右僕射，加侍中，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right and given the additional title Attendant-in-Ordinary; his generalship remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year he was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right and Attendant-in-Ordinary; his generalship was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年三月，復儀同三司，疾病未拜，見裴郭為祟。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first Shengui year, he was again granted Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies but did not take the appointment because of illness, and saw Pei and Guo as demons.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Shengui 1 he was again made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies but, ill, did not take office; he saw Pei and Guo as demons.

sentences.zh: 忠自知必死，表曰：「先帝錄臣父子一介之誠，昭臣家世奉公之節，故申之以婚姻，重之以爵祿，至乃位亞三槐，秩班九命。

translations.literal: Knowing he would surely die, Zhong submitted a memorial saying: "The late emperor recorded my father and myself for our single mote of loyalty, displayed my family's generations of public service, and therefore extended us marriage ties and heaped upon us titles and stipends, until my rank stood next to the Three Tree Lords and my grade matched the Nine Orders.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing death was near, Zhong memorialized: "The late emperor recognized my family's loyalty across generations, joined us to the throne by marriage, and heaped rank and stipend upon us until I stood next to the Three Tree Lords with grade matching the Nine Orders.

sentences.zh: 自大明利見之始，百官總己之初，臣復得猥攝禁戎，緝寧內外，斯誠社稷之靈，兆民之福，臣何力之有焉。

translations.literal: From when the Great Brightness first appeared and the hundred officials gathered their duties, I again had the humble charge of commanding the forbidden guard and keeping inner and outer realms at peace—truly the spirit of the altars of soil and grain and the fortune of the myriad people; what strength had I in it?
translations.idiomatic: From the day the late emperor took the throne I again commanded the palace guard and kept the realm at peace—a blessing to the state, not my doing.

sentences.zh: 但陛下以叡明御宇，皇太后以聖善臨朝，衽席不遺，簪屨弗棄，復乃寵窮出內，榮遍宮闈，[8]外牧兩河，入參百揆。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty governs the realm with penetrating wisdom and the empress dowager administers the court with sagely goodness, forgetting none at the sleeping mat and discarding not even hairpin and shoe attendants; then favor reached beyond the inner palace and glory filled the women's quarters, [8] governing the two river regions abroad and entering to join the hundred ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs with wisdom and the empress dowager with virtue, sparing none in the inner household; [8] I governed the two river regions abroad and served among the chief ministers at court.

sentences.zh: 顧服知妖，省躬識戾。

translations.literal: Looking at my garments I knew ill omens; examining myself I recognized my offenses.
translations.idiomatic: I saw omens in my dress and knew my own guilt.

sentences.zh: 而臣將慎靡方，致茲痾疚。

translations.literal: Yet I lacked proper caution and restraint, and brought on this grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: But I lacked restraint and brought on this grave illness.

sentences.zh: 自去秋苦痢，纏綿迄今，藥石備嘗，日增無損。

translations.literal: Since last autumn I have suffered dysentery, lingering until now; every medicine and remedy has been tried, yet day by day it grows worse without improvement.
translations.idiomatic: Since last autumn I have suffered dysentery without relief, though every remedy has been tried.

sentences.zh: 又今年已來，力候轉惡，微喘緒息，振復良難。

translations.literal: Moreover, from this year on my strength and vitality have turned worse; shallow breath with lingering respiration makes recovery very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: This year my strength has failed further; shallow breath makes recovery unlikely.

sentences.zh: 鴻慈未酬，伏枕涕咽。

translations.literal: Great kindness remains unrewarded; I weep upon my pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Your great kindness I cannot repay; I weep upon my pillow.

sentences.zh: 臣薄福無男，遺體莫嗣，貪及餘生，謹陳宿抱。

translations.literal: I have thin fortune and no son; my body has no heir; clinging to what remains of life, I respectfully state this long-held wish.
translations.idiomatic: I am poorly favored with no son to succeed me; clinging to what life remains, I state my long-held wish.

sentences.zh: 臣先養亡第四弟第二子司徒掾永超為子，猶子之念實切於心，乞立為嫡，傳此山河。

translations.literal: I previously adopted as my son Yongchao, the second son of my deceased fourth brother who served as a clerk in the Secretariat of State; the feeling for a nephew-son is truly deep in my heart. I beg that he be established as heir to inherit this fief.
translations.idiomatic: I earlier adopted Yongchao, second son of my late fourth brother and a clerk in the Secretariat, as my son; I beg that he be made heir to inherit this fief.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后令曰：「于忠表如此。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Yu Zhong's memorial reads thus.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered: "Yu Zhong's memorial reads as follows.

sentences.zh: 既誠勳宜錄，又無子可矜。

translations.literal: His loyal merit deserves recording, and he has no son to pity.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal service deserves reward, and he has no son of his own.

sentences.zh: 臨危所祈，不容致奪，可特聽如請，以彰殊效。

translations.literal: What he prayed for at the brink of death cannot be denied; specially grant his request to display exceptional reward.
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed plea cannot be refused; grant it specially to honor his service.

sentences.zh: 」忠薨，年五十七。

translations.literal: " Zhong died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢二十萬、布七百匹、蠟三百斤，贈侍中、司空公。

translations.literal: He was given Eastern Garden secret coffin fittings, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, two hundred thousand coins, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax; posthumously honored as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He received Eastern Garden secret coffin fittings, court robes, a suit of clothes, two hundred thousand coins, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax, and was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「太常少卿元端議，忠剛直猛暴，專戇好殺，案諡法剛強理直曰『武』，怙威肆行曰『醜』，宜諡武醜公。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "Vice Director of Ceremonials Yuan Duan proposed that Zhong was rigid, straight, fierce, and violent, willfully stubborn and fond of killing. According to posthumous-name standards, 'rigid and strong with straight principle' yields Wu and 'relying on power to act wantonly' yields Chou; he should be posthumously named Duke Wu-Chou.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported: Vice Director of Ceremonials Yuan Duan argued that Zhong was fierce, violent, and willfully fond of killing; by posthumous-name law, "rigid and strong with straight principle" yields Wu and "relying on power to act wantonly" yields Chou—he should be styled Duke Wu-Chou.

sentences.zh: 太常卿元脩義議，忠盡心奉上，剪除凶逆，依諡法除偽寧真曰『武』，夙夜恭事曰『敬』，諡武敬公。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonials Yuan Xiuyi proposed that Zhong devoted himself to serving the ruler and eliminated the wicked and rebellious. According to posthumous-name standards, 'removing falsehood and settling truth' yields Wu and 'diligent service day and night' yields Jing; he should be posthumously named Duke Wu-Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonials Yuan Xiuyi argued that Zhong served the ruler faithfully and cut down the wicked; by posthumous-name law, "removing falsehood and settling truth" yields Wu and "diligent service day and night" yields Jing—he should be styled Duke Wu-Jing.

sentences.zh: 二卿不同。

translations.literal: The two directors differed.
translations.idiomatic: The two directors disagreed.

sentences.zh: 」事奏，靈太后令曰：「可依正卿議。」

translations.literal: " When the matter was reported, Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Follow the senior director's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Follow the senior director's proposal."

sentences.zh: 于氏自曾祖四世貴盛，一皇后，四贈三公，領軍、尚書令，三開國公。

translations.literal: From their great-grandfather the Yu clan for four generations was noble and flourishing: one empress, four posthumous Grand Dukes, commanders of the guards and Director of the Masters of Writing, and three founding marquises.
translations.idiomatic: From the great-grandfather's generation the Yu clan flourished for four generations: one empress, four posthumous Grand Dukes, commanders of the guards and Director of the Masters of Writing, and three founding marquises.

sentences.zh: [9]忠性多猜忌，不交勝己，唯與直閤將軍章初瓌、千牛備身楊保元為斷金之交。

translations.literal: [9] Zhong was by nature much given to suspicion and jealousy; he would not associate with those who surpassed him. Only with General of the Direct Gate Zhang Chugui and Palace Guard Attendant Yang Baoyuan did he share a bond firm as fused metal.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Zhong was suspicious by nature and kept company only with men he could not surpass; his sworn friends were General of the Direct Gate Zhang Chugui and Palace Guard Attendant Yang Baoyuan.

sentences.zh: 李世哲求寵於忠，私以金帛寶貨事初瓌、保元，初瓌、保元談之，遂被賞愛，引為腹心。

translations.literal: Li Shizhe sought Zhong's favor and privately offered gold, silk, and precious goods to Chugui and Baoyuan; Chugui and Baoyuan spoke for him, and he was then prized and loved and brought in as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhe sought Zhong's favor by secretly giving gold, silk, and treasures to Chugui and Baoyuan; they spoke for him, and he became a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 忠擅權昧進，為崇訓之由，皆世哲計也。

translations.literal: Zhong's monopoly of power, blind advancement, and the reason for the Chongxun title were all Li Shizhe's schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's seizure of power, reckless promotions, and the Chongxun affair were all Li Shizhe's doing.

sentences.zh: 忠後妻中山王尼須女，微解詩書，靈太后臨朝，引為女侍中，賜號范陽郡君。

translations.literal: Zhong's later wife was the daughter of Prince Zhongshan Ni; she had some knowledge of poetry and books. When Empress Dowager Ling administered the court, she was brought in as Lady Attendant and granted the title Lady of Fanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's later wife was a daughter of Prince Zhongshan Ni and knew something of poetry and books; when Empress Dowager Ling took power she was made Lady Attendant and titled Lady of Fanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永超名翻，襲爵。

translations.literal: Yongchao's name was Fan; he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchao, styled Fan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 子世衡，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shiheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, titles were reduced by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, titles were reduced by regulation.

sentences.zh: 忠弟景，字百年。

translations.literal: Zhong's younger brother Jing, styled Bainian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's younger brother Jing, styled Bainian.

sentences.zh: 自司州從事，稍遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: From Assistant in Si Province he gradually rose to Colonel of Footmen.
translations.idiomatic: From Assistant in Si Province he rose to Colonel of Footmen.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、高平鎮將。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North and garrison commander of Gao-ping.
translations.idiomatic: He was General Who Pacifies the North and commander of Gao-ping Garrison.

sentences.zh: 坐貪殘受納，為御史中尉王顯所彈，會赦免。

translations.literal: Because of greedy cruelty and accepting bribes, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian and was pardoned at an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian for extortion and bribery but pardoned at an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 忠薨後，景為武衞將軍。

translations.literal: After Zhong's death, Jing became General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong died, Jing became General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 謀廢元叉，叉黜為征虜將軍、懷荒鎮將。

translations.literal: He plotted to depose Yuan Cha; Cha demoted him to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and garrison commander of Huaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to depose Yuan Cha; Cha demoted him to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and commander of Huaihuang Garrison.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕主阿那瓌叛亂，鎮民固請糧廩，而景不給。

translations.literal: When the Rouran ruler Anagui rebelled, the garrison people repeatedly requested grain from the granaries, but Jing would not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran ruler Anagui rebelled, the garrison people repeatedly asked for grain from the stores, but Jing refused.

sentences.zh: 鎮民不勝其忿，遂反叛。

translations.literal: The garrison people, unable to bear their rage, then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear their anger, the garrison people rebelled.

sentences.zh: 執縛景及其妻，拘守別室，皆去其衣服，令景著皮裘，妻著故絳襖。

translations.literal: They seized and bound Jing and his wife, confined them in separate rooms, stripped them of their clothes, made Jing wear a fur robe, and his wife wear an old crimson jacket.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Jing and his wife, held them in separate rooms, stripped them, made Jing wear a fur robe and his wife an old crimson jacket.

sentences.zh: 其被毀辱如此。

translations.literal: They were humiliated in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the humiliation they suffered.

sentences.zh: 月餘，乃殺之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, they killed them.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later they killed them.

sentences.zh: 烈弟敦，自中散遷驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Dun rose from Attendant to General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's younger brother Dun rose from Attendant to General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 景明中，假節，行并州事，除征虜將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he held the staff of authority and acted for Bing Province, was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he held the staff of authority and acted for Bing Province, and was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈使持節、平北將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously honored as Commissioner Bearing the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Commissioner Bearing the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 子昕，員外郎，直後，主衣都統，揚烈將軍，懷朔、武川鎮將，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His son Xin served as Outer Section Officer, Attendant Behind the Throne, Director of the Master of Robes Corps, General Who Exalts Merit, garrison commander of Huai-shuo and Wuchuan, and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin served as Outer Section Officer, Attendant Behind the Throne, Director of the Master of Robes Corps, General Who Exalts Merit, commander of Huai-shuo and Wuchuan Garrisons, and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，使蠕蠕，與阿那瓌擒逆賊破洛汗聽明、出六斤等。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was sent to the Rouran and with Anagui captured the rebel bandits Polohan Tingming, Chuliujin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he was sent to the Rouran and with Anagui captured the rebels Polohan Tingming, Chuliujin, and others.

sentences.zh: 轉輔國將軍、北中郎將、恒州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Supports the State, General of the North Gentlemen, and Chief Rectifier of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Supports the State, General of the North Gentlemen, and Chief Rectifier of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 又遷撫軍將軍、衞尉卿。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to General Who Calms the Army and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Calms the Army and Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮東將軍，殷、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posted out as General Who Garrisons the East and Inspector of Yin and Heng Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General Who Garrisons the East and Inspector of Yin and Heng Provinces.

sentences.zh: 還拜征東將軍，領左右。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was made General Who Conquers the East and head of the Left and Right Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made General Who Conquers the East and head of the Left and Right Corps.

sentences.zh: 天平中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Tianping era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Tianping era.

sentences.zh: 贈都督冀定州諸軍事、衞將軍、尚書僕射、儀同三司，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Commander-in-Chief of Ji and Ding Provinces, Guard General, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies; posthumously styled Wen-Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Commander-in-Chief of Ji and Ding Provinces, Guard General, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies; posthumously styled Wen-Gong.

sentences.zh: 長子揚仁。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Yangren.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Yangren.

sentences.zh: 武定中，勃海太守。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Prefect of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was Prefect of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 揚仁弟叉羅，字仲綱。

translations.literal: Yangren's younger brother Chaluo, styled Zhonggang.
translations.idiomatic: Yangren's younger brother Chaluo, styled Zhonggang.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: General of the Central Army and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was General of the Central Army and Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 叉羅弟子榮，魯郡太守。

translations.literal: Chaluo's younger brother's son Rong was Prefect of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chaluo's nephew Rong was Prefect of Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 敦弟果，嚴毅直亮，有父兄之風。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Guo was stern, resolute, upright, and bright, with his father's and brothers' bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Guo was stern, resolute, upright, and bright, with his father and brothers' character.

sentences.zh: 自中散稍遷光祿大夫，守尚書，賜爵武城子。

translations.literal: From Attendant he gradually rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Director of the Masters of Writing, and was granted the title Marquis of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: From Attendant he rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Director of the Masters of Writing, and was granted the title Marquis of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 太和中，歷朔、華、并、恒四州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he successively served as Inspector of Shuo, Hua, Bing, and Heng Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he served in turn as Inspector of Shuo, Hua, Bing, and Heng Provinces.

sentences.zh: 子礫，襲。

translations.literal: His son Li inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li succeeded.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人，通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Attendant of the Crown Prince and General Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was Attendant of the Crown Prince and General Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰哀。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously honored as General of the Right and Inspector of Luo Province; posthumously styled Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of the Right and Inspector of Luo Province; posthumously styled Ai.

sentences.zh: 子暉，征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Hui was General Who Conquers the East and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui was General Who Conquers the East and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel.

sentences.zh: 暉弟道揚，儀同開府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Daoyang was Equal in Honor Staff Opening Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Daoyang was Equal in Honor Staff Opening Consultant.

sentences.zh: 礫弟祇，卒於司徒掾。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Qi died as Clerk of the Secretariat of State.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Qi died while serving as Clerk of the Secretariat of State.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮遠將軍、朔州刺史，諡曰悼。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Shuo Province; posthumously styled Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Shuo Province; posthumously styled Dao.

sentences.zh: 祇子元伯，中散大夫。

translations.literal: Qi's son Yuanbo was Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's son Yuanbo was Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 果弟勁，事在外戚傳。

translations.literal: Guo's younger brother Jin—his story is in the Biographies of the Empresses' Clans.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's younger brother Jin is treated in the Biographies of the Empresses' Clans.

sentences.zh: 勁弟須，中散。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Xu was Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Xu was Attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷長水校尉，稍遷武衞將軍、太府卿、鎮南將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Colonel of the Long River and gradually rose to General of the Martial Guard, Minister of the Grand Storehouse, General Who Garrisons the South, and Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Colonel of the Long River, then to General of the Martial Guard, Minister of the Grand Storehouse, General Who Garrisons the South, and Inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中、車騎大將軍、尚書右僕射、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously honored as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 冀州長史。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was Chief Administrator of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征南將軍、燕州刺史，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Yan Province; posthumously styled Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Yan Province; posthumously styled Wu.

sentences.zh: 子翊，太尉從事中郎、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yi was Attendant in the Secretariat of the Grand Commandant and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was Attendant in the Secretariat of the Grand Commandant and Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 子長文，字士端。

translations.literal: Yi's son Zhangwen, styled Shiduan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Zhangwen, styled Shiduan.

sentences.zh: 武定中，尚書考功郎。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Director of the Bureau of Evaluation of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was Director of the Bureau of Evaluation of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 須弟文仁，太中大夫。

translations.literal: Xu's younger brother Wenren was Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's younger brother Wenren was Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魏定中原，于栗磾有武功於三世。

translations.literal: The historian says: When Wei settled the Central Plains, Yu Lidi had military merit over three reigns.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Wei settled the Central Plains, Yu Lidi won military glory across three reigns.

sentences.zh: 兼以虛己下物，罰不濫加，斯亦諸將所希矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, he emptied himself to defer to others and did not punish wantonly—this too is what generals rarely achieve.
translations.idiomatic: He also humbled himself before others and did not punish wantonly—rare among generals.

sentences.zh: 拔任參內外，以著能名。

translations.literal: Ba was appointed in both inner and outer posts and thereby made a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Ba served in inner and outer posts and won a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 烈氣概沉遠，受任艱危之際，有柱石之質，殆禦侮之臣。

translations.literal: Lie had a spirit deep and far-reaching; entrusted at a time of peril, he had the quality of a pillar—indeed a minister who repelled insult to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lie had a deep and steady spirit; in crisis he had the quality of a pillar—a minister who could repel insult to the state.

sentences.zh: 忠以骾朴見親，乘非其據，遂擅威權，生殺自己。

translations.literal: Zhong was favored for his rugged honesty; seizing power unworthily, he then monopolized authority and held life and death in his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was favored for blunt honesty but seized power unworthily, monopolizing authority with life and death at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 苟非女主之世，何以全其門族？

translations.literal: Had it not been an age of female rule, how could his clan have been spared?
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been an age of female rule, how could his house have survived intact?

sentences.zh: 其不誅滅，抑天幸也。

translations.literal: That they were not exterminated was merely heaven's luck.
translations.idiomatic: That they were not destroyed was merely heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes.

sentences.zh: 都督兗相二州諸軍事 諸本「相」作「桓」。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief of Yan and Xiang Provinces: in various editions "Xiang" is written "Huan."
translations.idiomatic: On "Commander-in-Chief of Yan and Xiang Provinces": various editions read Xiang as Huan.

sentences.zh: 按魏無「桓州」。

translations.literal: Note: Wei had no "Huan Province."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Wei had no Huan Province.

sentences.zh: 下列官銜又有「枋頭都將」，枋頭在相州，「桓」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Among the following titles there is also "Commander at Fangtou"; Fangtou lies in Xiang Province—the character "Huan" is erroneous, and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Later titles also include "Commander at Fangtou"; Fangtou is in Xiang Province, so Huan is a scribal error and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 所由遣私奴索官家羽林 御覽卷四二八

translations.literal: The official sent private slaves to demand imperial guards  Imperial Readings, vol. 428.
translations.idiomatic: Collation entry: "The official sent private slaves to demand imperial guards" — Imperial Readings, vol. 428.

sentences.zh: 〈一九七０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 1970〉
translations.idiomatic: (Imperial Readings, p. 1970)

sentences.zh: 「所由」作「何由」。

translations.literal: "Suoyou" is written "Heyou."
translations.idiomatic: Various editions read suoyou as heyou.

sentences.zh: 按「所由」常見於唐代文書，指主管的官吏，魏時罕見，疑作「何由」是。

translations.literal: We note that "suoyou" commonly appears in Tang documents, referring to the supervising official; it is rare in Wei times—suspected that writing "heyou" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Suoyou commonly denotes the responsible official in Tang documents but is rare in Wei texts; heyou is probably correct here.

sentences.zh: 會二年正月礿祭 諸本「礿」作「初」。

translations.literal: At the Yue sacrifice in the first month of the second year. In all editions "Yue" is written "chu."
translations.idiomatic: On the Yue sacrifice in the first month, year 2: all editions miswrite Yue as chu.

sentences.zh: 按卷二一上咸陽王禧傳、卷二一下彭城王勰傳都作「礿祭」。

translations.literal: We note that juan 21a, Biography of Prince of Xianyang Xi, and juan 21b, Biography of Prince of Pengcheng Xie, both read "Yue sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Both the Xianyang Wang Xi and Pengcheng Wang Xie biographies (juan 21) read Yue sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一四四

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian juan 144
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian juan 144

sentences.zh: 〈四四八二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 4482〉

sentences.zh: 也作「礿祭」。

translations.literal: Also reads "Yue sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: also reads Yue sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 「礿」是皇帝春祭宗廟之名，「初」乃形訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Yue" is the name of the emperor's spring sacrifice to the ancestral temple; "chu" is a graphic error—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Yue is the emperor's spring temple sacrifice; chu is a graphic error and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 尋除左右郎將 北史卷二三于忠傳、御覽卷二四０

translations.literal: Soon appointed General of the Left and Right. Beishi juan 23, Biography of Yu Zhong; Yulan juan 240
translations.idiomatic: Soon made General of the Left and Right: Beishi juan 23 (Yu Zhong), Yulan juan 240

sentences.zh: 〈一一三八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 1138〉
"Right" is written "central."
translations.idiomatic: Right is written as central.

sentences.zh: 按「左右郎將」乃左中郎將和右中郎將的合稱，疑作「左中郎將」是。

translations.literal: We note that "Generals of the Left and Right" is the combined designation for General of the Central Command of the Left and General of the Central Command of the Right; suspected that writing "General of the Central Command of the Left" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of the Left and Right denotes both left and right central commanders; left central commander alone is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 又自矯旨為儀同三司 諸本「矯」下脫「旨」字，今據北史卷二三于忠傳、冊府卷五一九

translations.literal: Moreover on his own he forged an edict making himself Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies. In all editions beneath "forge" the character "edict" is missing; now supplemented according to Beishi juan 23, Biography of Yu Zhong, and Cefu juan 519
translations.idiomatic: Forged an edict making himself Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies: all editions omit zhi under jiao; restored per Beishi juan 23 (Yu Zhong) and Cefu juan 519

sentences.zh: 〈六二０六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 6206〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Restored.

sentences.zh: 崔光與忠雖同受召 冊府

translations.literal: Cui Guang and Zhong though both received summons. Cefu
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang and Zhong both received summons: Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Same juan, page〉
translations.idiomatic: (same juan and page)

translations.literal: "Summon" is written "edict."
translations.idiomatic: Summon is written as edict.

sentences.zh: 按崔光與于忠同在門下，上文說忠「乃諷朝廷，同在門下者皆加封邑」，所以說「雖同受詔」。

translations.literal: We note that Cui Guang and Yu Zhong were both in the Secretariat; above it says Zhong "thereupon prompted the court that all who shared the Secretariat should receive increased fiefs," hence the wording "though both received edicts."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang and Yu Zhong were both in the Secretariat; the text says Zhong had all Secretariat colleagues enfeoffed—hence both received edicts.

sentences.zh: 據傳文和卷六七崔光傳別無「同受召」的事。

translations.literal: According to the biography text and juan 67, Biography of Cui Guang, there is no other matter of "both receiving summons."
translations.idiomatic: Neither this biography nor juan 67 (Cui Guang) mentions both being summoned.

sentences.zh: 疑「召」字為「詔」之訛。

translations.literal: Suspected that the character "summon" is an error for "edict."
translations.idiomatic: Summon is probably a corruption of edict.

sentences.zh: 但忠以光意望崇重逼光 冊府

translations.literal: Only Zhong, because Guang's intent and prestige were lofty and weighty, compelled Guang. Cefu
translations.idiomatic: Zhong compelled Guang because of his prestige: Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Same juan, page〉
translations.idiomatic: (same juan and page)

sentences.zh: 「意望」作「聲望」，「逼光」下有「為助」二字。

translations.literal: "Intent and prestige" is written "voice and prestige"; beneath "compel Guang" are the two characters "as aid."
translations.idiomatic: Intent and prestige reads as voice and prestige; two characters for as aid follow compelled Guang.

sentences.zh: 按文義作「聲望」較長，「逼光」下有二字語意也較完足，疑此傳訛脫。

translations.literal: By textual sense "voice and prestige" is fuller; with two characters beneath "compel Guang" the meaning is also more complete—suspected that this biography has errors and omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Voice and prestige fits better, and the extra two characters complete the sense; this passage may have dropped text.

sentences.zh: 但如傳文亦可通，今不改。

translations.literal: Yet as the biography text stands it can also be understood; not changed now.
translations.idiomatic: The received text is intelligible as it stands; left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 榮遍宮闈 諸本「闈」訛「閨」，今據冊府卷八六三

translations.literal: Glory filling the palace gates. In all editions "gates" is erroneous as "inner quarters"; now corrected according to Cefu juan 863
translations.idiomatic: Glory filling the palace gates: all editions miswrite wei as gui; corrected per Cefu juan 863

sentences.zh: 〈一０二五二頁〉
改。

translations.literal: Corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected.

sentences.zh: 于氏自曾祖四世貴盛一皇后四贈三公領軍尚書令三開國公 北史卷二三于栗磾附于勁傳後作「自栗磾至勁，累世貴盛，一皇后，四贈公，三領軍，二尚書令，三開國公」。

translations.literal: The Yu clan from great-grandfather for four generations was nobly prosperous—one empress, four posthumous Three Excellencies, Commander of the Guards, Director of the Masters of Writing, three founding dukes. Beishi juan 23, after the attached biography of Yu Jin in the biography of Yu Lidi, reads "From Lidi to Jin, generation after generation was nobly prosperous—one empress, four posthumous dukes, three Commanders of the Guards, two Directors of the Masters of Writing, three founding dukes."
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan flourished for four generations from the great-grandfather—one empress, four posthumous dukes, commanders of the guard, directors of the Masters of Writing, three founding dukes. Beishi juan 23, after Yu Jin, reads: from Lidi to Jin, generations of eminence—one empress, four posthumous dukes, three commanders of the guard, two directors of the Masters of Writing, three founding dukes.

sentences.zh: 本書于勁在卷八三下外戚傳下，外戚傳以北史補，故傳後語與北史同。

translations.literal: In this book Yu Jin is under juan 83b, Biographies of External Kin; the External Kin biographies are supplemented from Beishi, hence the words after the biography match Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin appears in juan 83b (External Kin), a section supplemented from Beishi—hence the closing lines match Beishi.

sentences.zh: 按這句話本當在忠傳後，北史移在勁傳後，實誤，別見卷八三下校記。

translations.literal: We note that this sentence ought originally to have followed the biography of Zhong; Beishi moved it after the biography of Jin—an actual error; see separately the collation notes to juan 83b.
translations.idiomatic: This sentence belonged after Zhong's biography; Beishi misplaced it after Jin's—see juan 83b collation notes.

sentences.zh: 這裏「領軍」和「尚書令」上脫去數目字。

translations.literal: Here above "Commander of the Guards" and "Director of the Masters of Writing" numerals are missing.
translations.idiomatic: Numerals are missing before Commander of the Guards and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 疑「三公」二字誤倒，當同北史作「四贈公，三領軍」，「尚書令」上脫「二」字。

translations.literal: Suspected that the two characters "Three Excellencies" are reversed in error; it should match Beishi as "four posthumous dukes, three Commanders of the Guards"; above "Director of the Masters of Writing" the character "two" is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Three Excellencies is probably transposed; it should read as in Beishi: four posthumous dukes, three commanders of the guard, with two missing before Director of the Masters of Writing.
